have long stalks (gǎo) and full ears,
large bases but slender stems,
sparse plantings but large ears;
their grains (sù) are round and have thin husks;
their rice is abundant (wò) and strong (qiáng) when eaten;
such crops are not affected by wind.
Those planted too early,
their stems and leaves have short awns (máng) and do not grow horizontally,
the ears are large but the fragrance is lost,
the rice is small (gǎo mǐ) and not fragrant.
Those planted too late,
their stems and leaves have awns (máng) but are stunted at the tip,
the ears are small and prematurely green,
many husks (pǐ) and not full.
Millet (shǔ) planted at the right time,
has awned (máng) stems and is slender at the bottom,
the ears are awned (máng) and long,
the rice is round (tuán) and has thin husks,
easy to hull,
and fragrant when eaten without irritation (huán);
such crops are not sticky (yí).
Those planted too early,
have large bases and luxuriant leaves,
stems are slender but do not mature,
leaves wither and ears are short.
Those planted too late,
have small stems and grow scraggily (má cháng),
short ears and thick husks,
the small rice is shrunken (qián) and not fragrant.
Rice (dào) planted at the right time,
has a large base and luxuriant stems,
long stalks (gǎo) and sparse plantings,
ears like a horse's tail,
large grains (lì) without awns (máng),
the rice is round (tuán) and has thin husks,
easy to hull and fragrant when eaten;
such crops are not husky (ài).
Those planted too early,
have large bases and stiffly opposing stems and leaves,
short stalks (gǎo) and short ears,
many husks (pǐ) and thick husks,
thin rice and many awns (máng).
Those planted too late,
have slender stems and do not thrive,
thick husks and many husks (pǐ), shrunken (pì) rice,
cannot rely on (dài) definite ripening,
they look up to heaven and die.
Hemp (má) planted at the right time,
must be awned (máng) and long,
sparse nodes and a sunny color,
small base but firm stems,
thick fibers (xǐ) and even,
ripens late with much glory,
grows again dividing day and night;
such crops are not affected by locusts (huáng).
Beans (shú) planted at the right time,
have long stems and short roots,
their beautiful pods form clusters (zú) of fourteen,
many branches and numerous nodes,
competing leaves and abundant fruit,
large beans are round,
small beans are compact (tuán) and fragrant,
heavy when weighed,
restorative (xī) and fragrant when eaten;
such crops are not affected by insects (chóng).
Those planted too early,
must grow long and vine-like,
floating leaves and sparse nodes,
small flowers (yīng) and unfruitful pods.
Those planted too late,
short stems and sparse nodes,
empty at the base and unfruitful.
Wheat (mài) planted at the right time,
has long stalks (gǎo) and black necks,
forming fourteen rows,
and conforming,
thin bran (sǔi) and red color,
heavy when weighed,
produces fragrance and sustenance (xī) when eaten,
making people's skin lustrous and strong;
such crops are not affected by maggots (qú jū).
Those planted too early,
swell (fú dòng) before the summer rains arrive,
infested with maggots (qú jū) and many diseases,
their secondary growth is limited by nodes.
Those planted too late,
have weak seedlings and grayish-green ears,
pale in color and with beautiful awns (máng).
Therefore, crops planted at the right time thrive,
crops planted at the wrong time are stunted.
If stems are similar when weighed,
those planted at the right time are heavier,
and have more grain (sù).
If grain (sù) quantities are similar when hulled,
those planted at the right time yield more rice.
If rice quantities are similar when eaten,
those planted at the right time are more filling.
Therefore, crops harvested at the proper time,
their aroma is fragrant,
their taste is sweet,
their qi is distinct,
if one eats them for a hundred days,
ears and eyes become keen,
heart and mind become profoundly wise,
the four defenses become strong,
malignant qi will not enter,
and the body will be free from severe calamity.
Huángdì said:
"When the four seasons are out of order,
one only needs to rectify the five grains."
